The questionnaire's information acquisition block lists exactly 7 sources and the table has exactly 7 items, so the counts agree, and every code is a column of Final_COVIDiSTRESS_Vol2_cleaned.csv. The tie between a given code and a given source is the questionnaire's listing order and nothing further, so the order within the block is not independently confirmed. This block appears in only one of the two questionnaire workbooks, so there is no second document to compare wording against.

The 6 misperception items are pinned individually: the questionnaire numbers them B.1.1 to B.3.2 and the codes run misperception1_1 to misperception3_2, so both block and within-block position are named at each end. The remaining 7 items (4 conspiratorial thinking, 3 anti-expert) rest on listing order with counts agreeing exactly at 4 and 3, so their order within each block is not independently confirmed. All 13 codes are columns of Final_COVIDiSTRESS_Vol2_cleaned.csv. The stated randomisation is independently visible: the questionnaire says 'randomly show 1 of each block (B)' and the 6 misperception items average n=6,561 against 13,069 for the other 7, a ratio of 0.502, confirming both the three-block structure and that B.x.1 and B.x.2 are alternatives within block x.

The three blocks are pinned by the table's own item_family column (1/2/3, 8 items each) together with the questionnaire's per-block wording ('Wash your hands' / 'Washing their hands' / 'Wash their hands'). Position 7 is pinned by a response fingerprint: it is the single reverse-worded behaviour and index 7 is the outlier in all three blocks, mean r against block-mates -0.09, +0.11 and -0.04 against +0.25 to +0.60 elsewhere. Wording is confirmed by both questionnaire workbooks agreeing word for word across all 18 lines. The other 7 positions within each block rest on listing order, so they are not individually confirmed. Block sizes are independently confirmed by the stated randomisation: each participant randomly received 2 of the 8 norm behaviours, and the norm blocks average n=3,794 and n=3,777 against n=15,081 for compliance over 15,607 respondents, a ratio of 0.251, i.e. 2 of 8.

The codebook names each of CESD1-CESD20 and pairs it with its own stem and its four numbered options, so every item is tied to its text by a label match, not an order inference, and all 20 share one response set. Independent of the codebook, the data confirm the tie at four positions: the canonical CES-D words items 4, 8, 12 and 16 positively, the shipped stems put the positive wording at exactly those numbers, and those four are the only items correlating negatively with the rest -- mean r against the other 19 of -0.293, -0.187, -0.277 and -0.293 against +0.224 to +0.339 for all sixteen others, with no overlap. validate_items.R reports item-set and resp-set matching live data (20 items, 15,471 rows).

The codebook names each of the 24 codes and pairs it with its own stem and numbered options, so every item is tied to its text by a label match rather than an order inference; 20 items carry the 0-3 difficulty run and 4 carry the yes/no aids run, and all 87 shipped option cells re-derive from the codebook. validate_items.R reports item-set and resp-set matching live data (24 items, 37,677 rows). Corroboration rather than a second pin: items sharing a numeric prefix, i.e. the instrument's activity category, cohere more than items across two categories, within-category mean r=0.582 over 16 pairs against 0.499 over 174 -- the predicted direction, with overlapping ranges because the HAQ index is strongly unidimensional.
